blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A report service renders an object graph with a recursive method and wraps the call as `try { return render(graph); } catch (Exception e) { log.warn("render failed", e); return "{}"; }`. A graph with a cycle in it reaches this code. What does the code that called it get?

options.text: The string "{}", since what the recursion throws is a subtype of the type the catch clause names
options.says: the recursion ends in StackOverflowError, which extends Error, not Exception

options.text: The string "{}", since the catch clause takes whatever the call inside the try throws
options.says: a catch clause takes only its type and that type's subclasses; Errors are not Exceptions

options.text: A StackOverflowError, since what the recursion throws is outside the type the catch clause names
options.says: StackOverflowError extends Error, so catch (Exception) lets it pass

options.text: A StackOverflowError, since no catch block can run once the thread is out of stack
options.says: catch (Throwable) does take a StackOverflowError; what the catch clause names decides

origin.section: A catch Clause Catches Its Type and Every Subtype

questions.stem: An upload handler runs `try { store.put(file); } catch (IOException e) { audit.record(file.name()); throw new UploadException("upload failed", e); }`. The store fails with IOException("disk full"), and audit.record then fails with IllegalStateException("audit DB down"). What reaches the handler's caller?

options.text: An UploadException caused by "disk full", since the throw statement at the end of the catch block still runs
options.says: audit.record throws before that statement is reached, so the UploadException is never created

options.text: An UploadException caused by "disk full", since the audit failure is attached to it as a suppressed exception
options.says: nothing is attached automatically in a catch block; the UploadException is never created

options.text: The IllegalStateException, with "disk full" nowhere in its trace, since it leaves the catch block in place of the exception being handled
options.says: an exception thrown in a catch block replaces the one being handled, which is dropped with the variable e

options.text: The IllegalStateException, with "disk full" as its cause, since it leaves the catch block while that exception is being handled
options.says: Java doesn't link a new exception to the one being handled; audit.record knows nothing of e, and the output shows cause: null

origin.section: An Exception Thrown in a catch Block Replaces the One Being Handled

questions.stem: A validator keeps `static final ValidationException INVALID = new ValidationException("invalid")` and runs `INVALID.fillInStackTrace(); throw INVALID;` on bad input. Request A fails validation, catches the exception and queues it for logging. Before the logger runs, request B, on another thread, fails validation too. What does A's log entry show?

options.text: Request A's own frames, since A's call recorded its trace into the shared object for good
options.says: fillInStackTrace() on the shared object replaces the trace A's caught exception carries

options.text: Request A's own frames, since A's throw recorded its stack into the object it threw
options.says: throw records nothing; the trace comes from the constructor or fillInStackTrace()

options.text: Request B's frames, since B's call recorded its trace into the shared object over A's
options.says: fillInStackTrace() on the shared object replaces the trace that A's caught exception carries

options.text: Request B's frames, since B's throw recorded its stack into the object it threw
options.says: throw records nothing; B's frames are there because B called fillInStackTrace() on the shared object

origin.section: The Stack Trace Is Recorded Where the Exception Is Created, Not Where It Is Thrown

questions.stem: A CSV importer reads each field with Integer.parseInt inside its own try/catch. Almost every field is valid. A colleague proposes moving the try blocks out of the per-field loop, to save the cost of entering them on every field. What does that save on the valid fields?

options.text: Nothing measurable, since a try block adds no instruction and is consulted only when something is thrown
options.says: javac writes an exception table that the JVM reads only on a throw; valid input cost what checking first did

options.text: Nothing measurable, since the JIT removes the try block's setup once the loop is compiled
options.says: there is no setup to remove: javac emits no instruction for entering a try

options.text: A few nanoseconds per field, since entering a try block registers a handler that leaving it removes
options.says: nothing is registered at run time; the handler is a row in the method's exception table

options.text: A few nanoseconds per field, since entering a try block records the stack in case of a throw
options.says: the stack is recorded when an exception is created, not when a try is entered

origin.section: Throwing Costs Microseconds, Mostly the Stack Trace; a try That Doesn't Throw Costs Nothing

concepts: StackOverflowError and OutOfMemoryError extend Error, so catch (Exception) lets them pass while catch (Throwable) takes them.
Entering a try block executes no instruction; the exception table is read only when something is thrown.
